'''Yurii Evgenievich Nesterov''' (Russian: Юрий Евгеньевич Нестеров) (born January 25, 1956) is a Russian mathematician, an internationally recognized expert in [[convex optimization]], especially in the development of efficient [[algorithms]] and [[numerical optimization]] analysis. He is currently a emeritus professor at the [[Université catholique de Louvain|University of Louvain]] (UCLouvain) and Corvinus University of Budapest, fractional professor at the [[Chinese University of Hong Kong, Shenzhen]] (CUHKSZ) and [[Shenzhen Loop Area Institute]].

==Biography==
In 1977, Yurii Nesterov graduated in [[applied mathematics]] at [[Moscow State University]]. From 1977 to 1992 he was a researcher at the [[Central Economic Mathematical Institute]] of the [[Russian Academy of Sciences]]. Since 1993, he has been working at [[Université catholique de Louvain|UCLouvain]], specifically in the Department of Mathematical Engineering from the [[Louvain School of Engineering]], [[Center for Operations Research and Econometrics]].

In 2024, Nesterov joined [[School of Data Science]] of the [[Chinese University of Hong Kong, Shenzhen]] and [[Shenzhen Loop Area Institute]] as fractional professor.<ref>{{Cite web |title=NESTEROV, Yurii {{!}} School of Data Science |url=https://sds.cuhk.edu.cn/en/teacher/1634 |access-date=2026-07-23 |website=sds.cuhk.edu.cn}}</ref>

==Academic work==
Nesterov is most famous for his work in convex optimization, including his 2004 book, considered a canonical reference on the subject.<ref>{{cite book|title = Introductory lectures on convex optimization : A basic course|last = Nesterov|first = Yurii|isbn=978-1402075537 |publisher=Kluwer Academic Publishers |year=2004|citeseerx = 10.1.1.693.855}}</ref> His main novel contribution is an accelerated version of [[gradient descent]] that converges considerably faster than ordinary gradient descent (commonly referred as Nesterov momentum, Nesterov Acceleration or [[Nesterov accelerated gradient]], in short — NAG).<ref>{{cite journal|last1=Nesterov|first1=Y|title=A method for unconstrained convex minimization problem with the rate of convergence <math>O(1/k^2)</math>|date=1983|journal=Doklady AN USSR|volume=269|pages=543–547}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal |last=Walkington |first=Noel J. |date=2023 |title=Nesterov's Method for Convex Optimization |url=https://epubs.siam.org/doi/10.1137/21M1390037 |journal=SIAM Review |language=en |volume=65 |issue=2 |pages=539–562 |doi=10.1137/21M1390037 |issn=0036-1445|url-access=subscription }}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://blogs.princeton.edu/imabandit/2013/04/01/acceleratedgradientdescent/|title = ORF523: Nesterov's Accelerated Gradient Descent|date = April 1, 2013|access-date = June 4, 2014|last = Bubeck|first = Sebastien}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://blogs.princeton.edu/imabandit/2014/03/06/nesterovs-accelerated-gradient-descent-for-smooth-and-strongly-convex-optimization/|title = Nesterov's Accelerated Gradient Descent for Smooth and Strongly Convex Optimization|last = Bubeck|first = Sebastien|date = March 6, 2014|access-date = June 4, 2014}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=The zen of gradient descent |url=https://blog.mrtz.org/2013/09/07/the-zen-of-gradient-descent.html |access-date=2023-05-13 |website=blog.mrtz.org}}</ref> This method, sometimes called "FISTA", was further developed by Beck & Teboulle in their 2009 paper "A Fast Iterative Shrinkage-Thresholding Algorithm for Linear Inverse Problems".<ref>{{Cite journal|last=Beck|first=Amir|last2=Teboulle|first2=Marc|date=2009-01-01|title=A Fast Iterative Shrinkage-Thresholding Algorithm for Linear Inverse Problems|url=https://epubs.siam.org/doi/abs/10.1137/080716542|journal=SIAM Journal on Imaging Sciences|volume=2|issue=1|pages=183–202|doi=10.1137/080716542|url-access=subscription}}</ref>

His work with [[Arkadi Nemirovski]] in their 1994 book<ref>{{cite book |title=Interior-Point Polynomial Algorithms in Convex Programming  |last1= Nesterov |first1=Yurii |first2=Nemirovskii |last2=Arkadii |year=1995 |publisher=Society for Industrial and Applied Mathematics |isbn=978-0898715156}}</ref> is the first to point out that the [[interior point method]] can solve [[convex optimization]] problems, and the first to make a systematic study of [[semidefinite programming]] (SDP). Also in this book, they introduced the [[self-concordant function]]s which are useful in the analysis of [[Newton's method]].<ref>{{cite book |title=Convex Optimization |last1= Boyd|first1=Stephen P.|first2=Lieven |last2=Vandenberghe |year=2004 |publisher=Cambridge University Press |isbn=978-0-521-83378-3 |url=https://web.stanford.edu/~boyd/cvxbook/bv_cvxbook.pdf |access-date=October 15, 2011}}</ref>

== Awards and honors ==
In 2000, Nesterov received the [[George B. Dantzig Prize|Dantzig Prize]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.siam.org/prizes/sponsored/dantzig.php |title =The George B. Dantzig Prize |year = 2000|access-date = December 12, 2014}}</ref>

In 2009, Nesterov won the [[John von Neumann Theory Prize]].<ref>{{cite web|url = https://www.informs.org/Recognize-Excellence/Award-Recipients/Yurii-Nesterov|title = John Von Neumann Theory Prize|year = 2009|access-date = June 4, 2014|archive-date = February 22, 2014|archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20140222154015/https://www.informs.org/Recognize-Excellence/Award-Recipients/Yurii-Nesterov|url-status = dead}}</ref>

In 2016, Nesterov received the [[EURO Gold Medal]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.euro-online.org/web/pages/608/last-activities-list|title = EURO Gold Medal|year = 2016|access-date = August 20, 2016}}</ref>

In 2023, Yurii Nesterov and [[Arkadi Nemirovski]] received the WLA Prize in Computer Science or Mathematics, "for their seminal work in convex optimization theory".<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.thewlaprize.org/PressRoom/News/2023/09/14/179.html|title = Laureates of the 2023 WLA Prize Announced|year = 2023|access-date = October 4, 2023}}</ref>

In 2026, Nesterov was awarded the [[Carl Friedrich Gauss Prize]] by the IMU at the ICM 2026.<ref>[https://www.mathunion.org/imu-awards/carl-friedrich-gauss-prize/carl-friedrich-gauss-prize-2026 Carl Friedrich Gauss Prize 2026]</ref>
